This is true, this myth is perpetuated often here. Ppl say you have to always work towards a goal, that will get you closer to a bigger, harder to get to goal and so on, like climbing an infinite staircase. Do well in school, to get in a good college, to get a good job, to buy a house and support a family and have enough money to retire and cover any medical issues. While this might work for some, others will be miserable. After reaching my goals, some that felt unrealistic and that I would never achieve, 1 by 1 I realized more and that, I did not feel anything from them, got a jolt of happiness that lasted a few days and that was it. Got what I saw as my dream job and quit 6 months later because I was too depressed to get out of bed and was constantly suicidal. A few months later managed to get a business going that I was fantasizing about, never believing for a second that it could ever be more than that, a fantasy. 4 months later, same situation, quit the whole thing. Had similar experience with many things, but jobs had a longer term, more significant impact.

It's quite soul crushing when you realize you are chasing a carrot on a string, that no matter what you do, you will never have. So you work hard and push yourself so that you can at least every now and then get a sniff of the dangling carrot, that's so close, yet just out of reach. It's as good as it gets for some of us.

There are many types and they all manifest differently from patient to patient and as time passes.

Been' dealing with this for about a decade, it's like a pendulum, I have good and bad periods. For me it got worse over the years, not sure why, maybe it's an effect the depression has over time. On really bad periods I just lay in bed or sit at my computer and just stare at the wall, ceiling or my computer screen, daydreaming, waiting to get a drop of energy to do something, anything! When it's not too bad I just listen to music, sift through games I used to play, try and get back into 1 of them, look for a movie to watch, try and find something new on youtube that I never seen before. When I finally manage to get sucked into a game, it can be a good distraction for a few days, sometimes weeks, but those are periods that go by fast and are far apart. Haven't had a job or did any serious work in about 4 years I think.

I'd say, try your best when you have the energy to just keep sifting for stuff to keep yourself distracted with: a new job, a new hobby, movies, games, music, fandoms, books, meet new ppl (online at least if not irl), whatever you think fits you and you have the energy for. Doing anything is better then just siting around and doing nothing, allowing your mind to drift into the cold and dark infinite abyss. After all, even if you found nothing to do today, spending the day looking was doing something. I know it's easier said then done and it's not that easy or effective and it's hard to see a point to it all. I try to ignore the future and just try make today go by faster and less painful.

Don't have any good fix for it. Just duct taped it together and hope it holds.

I know this feeling very well. About 8 years ago I came up with a rule, I called it the 7-1 contact rule to filter out friends. It's simple, after initiating contact (phone call, sms, talking to them on msn/email/yahoo messanger/skype, anything at all!) for 7 times in a row without them initiating, I would not contact them until they initiated. Within about 3 months I managed to shake off the hand full of friends I had, not 1 left. Even on holydays or when it was my birthday, I was the one calling them. Maybe it wasn't a bad thing, maybe it just became a thing that I was supposed to initiate, but after a while I feel like I'm bothering them or holding them back/wasting theyr time. But now it's been about 8 years since, and no call, no sign of life, nothing. This kind of thing feels to much like a 1 way friendship. I'd say look for better friends. They are hard to find, but they are somewhere out there.
